# **Game Architecture and Technical Design Specification: Backyard Havoc**

## **1\. System Mechanics and Core Loop Dynamics**

### **1.1 Impulse Mechanics and Trajectory Mathematics**

The foundational interaction model of *Backyard Havoc* translates discrete screen touch or mouse click inputs into continuous physical momentum applied to a spherical projectile. The underlying physics engine models the projectile as a rigid 2D circular body operating within a Newtonian vector space1. When a user generates an input at screen coordinates ![][image1] relative to the projectile centroid ![][image2], the engine computes a directional impulse vector ![][image3] that governs the ball's immediate trajectory1.  
The raw directional displacement vector ![][image4] is calculated via vector subtraction:  
![][image5]  
To ensure numerical stability and prevent extreme impulse scaling when screen inputs occur near the center of mass, the directional vector is normalized to its unit vector ![][image6]. If the spatial distance ![][image7] falls below a defined minimum interaction radius ![][image8], a clamping scalar is applied. The total linear impulse ![][image3] incorporates a baseline impulse magnitude ![][image9], an offset distance factor, and an active combo multiplier coefficient ![][image10]:  
![][image11]  
where ![][image12] denotes the combo sensitivity scalar (configured to ![][image13]). The resulting linear impulse alters the velocity vector ![][image14] of the body via the impulse-momentum theorem ![][image15], where ![][image16] specifies the mass of the active ball variant3.  
Rotational dynamics are governed by the off-center tangential component of the applied force vector1. The torque ![][image17] applied to the projectile is derived from the cross product of the contact offset vector ![][image18] and the tangential force ![][image19]:  
![][image20]  
The change in angular velocity ![][image21] over a simulation timestep ![][image22] is dictated by the moment of inertia for a uniform circular disk ![][image23]:  
![][image24]  
This angular velocity interacts with kinetic friction coefficients during surface impacts, creating dynamic spin effects that alter ricochet trajectories1.

### **1.2 Session Pacing and Behavioral Loop Integration**

The core gameplay loop converts vertical timing mechanics into horizontal spatial destruction through an escalating four-stage behavioral pipeline:

> 1. **Keepy-Uppy Juggling:** The player executes precise vertical timing taps below the falling projectile to build an active combo multiplier ![][image25] (![][image26])5. Each successful kick elevates visual trail intensity and increases audio feedback pitch by a semitone step.  
> 2. **Horizontal Deflection and Destruction:** The player intentionally alters the kick angle to bank the high-multiplier projectile sideways into destructible environmental props (e.g., glass windows, greenhouse panels, outdoor furniture)6.  
> 3. **Environmental Cascades and Dynamic NPC Reactions:** Prop fractures trigger secondary physical interactions (e.g., falling pots striking pets, gas grill ignitions), while an edge Large Language Model (LLM) service streams real-time dynamic dialogue to NPC speech bubbles6.  
> 4. **Metagame Currency Cash-In:** At session completion, accumulated destruction points scaled by the peak combo multiplier are converted into "Street Cred" currency to unlock specialized ball physics modifiers and new suburban environments.

During the initial minute of play, the interaction design emphasizes mechanical onboarding5. The environment remains mostly non-reactive while the player masters vertical survival physics. Audio cues scale upwards pitch-wise with every tap, and particle emission rates expand dynamically. Between minutes one and three, horizontal destructibles are highlighted. A slight miscalculation in tap offset propels the ball horizontally into a neighbor's greenhouse, triggering dynamic glass fragmentation6. The structural break initiates domino-style collateral events: falling glass strikes a flowerpot, which collapses onto a sleeping dog, scaring the animal into knocking over a lighted barbecue grill that sets off a localized grease explosion6.  
To enforce long-term player retention on Day 1 (D1), the game incorporates a system known as "The Neighborhood Hitlist." This mechanism provides daily deterministic layout seeds paired with specific trickshot objectives—such as banking off a garden ornament into a second-story window with a ![][image27] combo active—compelling players to compete on global seed-based leaderboards.

### **1.3 Mathematical Model of Game Feel and Camera Trauma**

To maximize sensory feedback ("juice") during multi-object destruction cascades without degrading touch input precision, the rendering engine implements a non-linear camera trauma decay model9. System trauma ![][image28] tracks global environmental destruction intensity9. Impact events add trauma additively based on kinetic energy transfer:  
![][image29]  
Trauma decays continuously over elapsed time ![][image30] via a linear rate ![][image31]9:  
![][image32]  
Translational offsets ![][image33] and rotational offsets ![][image34] applied to the rendering camera use a quadratic trauma exponent to ensure light hits feel subtle while massive explosions generate intense screen shake9:  
![][image35]  
Independent 1D Perlin noise functions ![][image36] sampled at frequency ![][image37] determine instantaneous camera offsets9:  
![][image38]  
![][image39]  
![][image40]  
Because offsets are applied strictly to the render camera's viewport matrix during the frame draw pass, the underlying physics collision coordinates remain unperturbed, keeping touch input detection accurate2.

## **2\. Metagame Structure and Physics Interactions**

### **2.1 Ball Physics Modifiers and Parameter Engineering**

Progression relies on unlocking specialized ball variants that alter core parameters inside the simulation world4. Each ball modifies fundamental mass density, elasticity (restitution ![][image41]), friction (![][image42]), and aerodynamic drag (![][image43]), while carrying environmental state flags4.

| Ball Variant | Mass Density (kg/m3) | Coefficient of Restitution (e) | Static / Kinetic Friction (μ) | Drag Coefficient (Cd​) | Environmental State Flags | Mechanical Characteristics & Tactical Role |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Standard Leather** | **![][image44]** | **![][image45]** | **![][image46]** | **![][image13]** | COLLIDE\_DEFAULT | Baseline trajectory handling; predictable vertical parabolic bounce profiles. |
| **Superball** | **![][image47]** | **![][image48]** | **![][image13]** | **![][image49]** | BOUNCE\_BOOST | Retains ![][image50] kinetic energy per impact; ricochets predictably inside dense structural spaces1. |
| **Wet Sponge** | **![][image51]** | **![][image52]** | **![][image53]** | **![][image54]** | SPLATTER\_MUD | Absorbs kinetic energy on impact; splatters mud on security cameras and vehicle glass to blind sensors. |
| **Flaming Ball** | **![][image55]** | **![][image56]** | **![][image57]** | **![][image58]** | IGNITE\_SURFACE | Applies ON\_FIRE thermal flags to wood and cloth props; triggers automated lawn sprinkler systems. |

Mathematically, the coefficient of restitution ![][image41] dictates the ratio of relative contextual velocity post-collision relative to pre-collision along the normal unit vector ![][image59]1:  
![][image60]  
Kinetic energy loss ![][image61] per collision is expressed as:  
![][image62]  
By configuring ![][image63] for the Superball variant, kinetic energy dissipation drops near zero, causing high-velocity multi-bank ricochets in enclosed structures like greenhouses or garages1.

### **2.2 Environmental Escalation and Destruction Cascades**

Level progression follows an escalating structural topology. Initial stages take place in a Suburban Backyard, which emphasizes horizontal ground-level destruction targeting single-pane glass, wooden fences, and garden ornaments. Secondary environments transition to Balconies & Rooftops, shifting gameplay focus to verticality, steep gravity drops, satellite dish deflectors, and linked solar panel arrays. The tertiary level environment, the Luxury Marina, introduces high-density floating structures, wine glass towers governed by stacking constraints, dynamic motorboats, and security laser arrays.  
Environmental destruction relies on a threshold-based force propagation network3. When the kinetic energy ![][image64] delivered by a ball collision exceeds an object's structural yield threshold ![][image65], the original static body is removed from the physics world3. The engine replaces the body with a cluster of dynamic convex polygon fragments, scaling their initial velocities by the incoming impact vector and applying thermal (ON\_FIRE) or fluid (WET) state tags to adjacent bodies3.

## **3\. Real-Time Edge AI Integration and Procedural Systems**

### **3.1 Runtime Edge LLM Pipeline for NPC Dialogue**

To eliminate repetitive canned responses from dynamic gameplay, *Backyard Havoc* routes real-time physics telemetry to an edge LLM infrastructure (such as the Groq API running pruned LLaMA 3.3 70B models)7. The client engine serializes impact event sequences and transmits them asynchronously over persistent WebSocket connections7.

#### **Telemetry Event Schema Transmitted by Client Engine**

JSON  
{  
  "timestamp": 1711984200120,  
  "npc\_id": "grumpy\_neighbor\_kevin",  
  "npc\_persona": "Grumpy suburban gardener obsessive about prize-winning hydrangeas",  
  "trigger\_event": "DESTRUCTION",  
  "impact\_object": "Prize Hydrangea Garden & Birdbath",  
  "combo\_multiplier": 7,  
  "ball\_type": "Flaming Ball",  
  "ball\_velocity": 42.8,  
  "environmental\_tags": \["ON\_FIRE", "GARDEN\_RUINED"\]  
}

#### **Enforced Edge Output Schema**

The remote edge worker processes the incoming event stream, enforcing structured JSON mode outputs7. The end-to-end execution pipeline targets latency under 200 milliseconds to match real-time animation constraints8.

JSON  
{  
  "npc\_id": "grumpy\_neighbor\_kevin",  
  "dialogue\_text": "My hydrangeas\! You turned my prize-winning hydrangeas into a backyard bonfire, Kevin\!",  
  "emotion\_state": "RAGE",  
  "audio\_pitch\_modifier": 1.35,  
  "display\_duration\_sec": 2.5  
}

The game client receives this payload and instantiates an animated speech bubble positioned over the NPC's world coordinate transform7. If network latency exceeds the 200ms frame deadline, the system seamlessly plays a local, pre-rendered vocal grunt sound while queuing the text bubble render pass7.

### **3.2 AI Layout Director**

To keep layout setups varied across play sessions, an AI Layout Director monitors player skill telemetry using a four-dimensional vector:  
![][image66]  
When generating a level layout, the director adjusts prop spacing, target gap distances, dynamic deflector velocities, and breaking thresholds ![][image65]. Players demonstrating low precision receive wider receptive collateral zones and lower structural break thresholds. Conversely, high-skill profiles encounter narrower ricochet corridors, moving targets (e.g., automated lawnmowers), kinetic deflectors, and protected structural nodes requiring precise multi-bank trickshots.

## **4\. Reference Game Taxonomy and Comparative Analysis**

### **4.1 Cross-Genre Synthesis**

*Backyard Havoc* synthesizes core design elements from three distinct game design paradigms5:

* **Classic Flash Keepy-Uppy Games:** Contributes the timing-driven input loop of maintaining vertical ball momentum via screen taps5. The key shift replaces purely vertical survival goals with directional deflection targeting environmental props.  
* **Peggle & PAIN:** Contributes cascading score multipliers, pinball destruction mechanics, and multi-object variation scoring bonuses6. Rather than launching a single projectile from a stationary launcher, the player continuously juggles the ball to sustain chaotic physical cascades6.  
* **Untitled Goose Game:** Contributes sandbox mischief themes, grumpy NPC character dynamic reactions, and contextual objective structures17. The slow, stealth-focused interaction loop is converted into a high-tempo arcade sports destruction loop.

### **4.2 Comprehensive Comparative Framework**

| Design Axis | Classic Flash Keepy-Uppy | Peggle / PAIN | Untitled Goose Game | Backyard Havoc |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Primary Input Model** | Single-axis vertical timing taps5. | Stationary single launch vector setup6. | Free-roam 3D character navigation. | Multi-axis directional tap impulses during real-time juggling1. |
| **Physics Engine Integration** | Basic 1D/2D linear gravity translation1. | 2D rigid body constraints and ragdoll physics6. | Kinematic character controller with prop interactions. | 2D rigid body physics (Matter.js) with dynamic fracture mechanics1. |
| **Environmental System** | Static 2D background canvas; non-reactive1. | Semi-static peg boards and city props6. | Systemic stealth sandbox environment. | Dynamic physical structures with linked thermal and fluid propagation. |
| **NPC Behavior** | None. | Static target animations / Rigid ragdoll pathing6. | Node-based AI state machines. | Dynamic Edge LLM real-time commentary and speech bubble generation7. |
| **Score Engine** | Linear count increment (![][image67]). | Peg clearing and drop bucket multipliers6. | Objective checklist completion. | Multiplier cascades (![][image68])6. |

## **5\. Monetization Strategy and Soft Launch Metrics**

### **5.1 Ethical Microtransaction Engine**

Monetization is built entirely around cosmetics and level expansions, strictly avoiding pay-to-win modifiers or energy timers. Players can purchase custom ball skins (e.g., Disco Ball, Eyeball, Pixel Cube), particle kick trails (e.g., Rainbows, Electric Lightning, Flame Jets), and pop-art impact text overlays ("BAM\!", "KAPOW\!", "CRASH\!"). Content expansions offer themed neighborhood environments (e.g., Haunted Victorian Yard, Sci-Fi Lunar Base) bundled with unique destructible props, NPC archetypes, and dynamic vocal libraries.

### **5.2 Soft Launch Key Performance Indicators**

| Telemetry Metric | Target Goal | Soft Launch Kill Threshold | Churn Diagnostics & Mechanical Remediation Vectors |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Day 1 Retention (D1)** | **![][image69]** | **![][image70]** | **Diagnostic:** Churn indicates overly punishing juggle mechanics or insufficient visual feedback11. **Remediation:** Expand input hitboxes, increase base ball elasticity, and intensify screen shake trauma9. |
| **Runs per Active User (RPAU)** | **![][image71]** | **![][image72]** | **Diagnostic:** Low run counts indicate repetitive physics outcomes or weak progression goals. **Remediation:** Expand prop cascade paths, randomize level layouts, and introduce daily "Neighborhood Hitlist" objectives. |
| **Average Session Length (ASL)** | **![][image73]** | **![][image74]** | **Diagnostic:** Short session lengths point to mechanical fatigue or flat difficulty scaling. **Remediation:** Introduce multi-stage destruction challenges, allow mid-session ball swaps, and rebalance level progression curves. |

## **6\. Engineering Implementation in Matter.js and HTML5 Canvas**

### **6.1 Simulation Engine Architecture**

The web prototype utilizes an HTML5 \<canvas\> rendering pipeline driven by Matter.js for 2D rigid body physics1. The physics simulation isolates world updates from rendering passes, running at a fixed 60 Hz update rate2.  
Key world setup values include a gravity vector of ![][image75]1, six position iteration passes per step, four velocity iteration passes per step, and two constraint iteration passes per step. Projectiles are instantiated as circular bodies (![][image76], density ![][image77], restitution ![][image78], friction ![][image79]) with Continuous Collision Detection (CCD) flags active2. Destructible props are represented as dynamic rectangle bodies (![][image80], density ![][image81]) set to static mode until an impact energy threshold is crossed4.

### **6.2 Mitigation of Fast-Moving Body Tunneling**

A recurring issue in discrete Euler-integrated physics engines like Matter.js is body tunneling1. When high impulses accelerate the ball beyond its spatial radius in a single frame (![][image82]), discrete collision checks can miss thin colliders entirely1.

Frame t:    ( Ball )  | Window |  
                      |        |  
Frame t+1:            | Window |  ( Ball )  \<-- TUNNELED\! (No collision registered)

To resolve tunneling without relying on heavy WASM physics binaries, the architecture combines sub-stepping updates with swept raycasting2:

> 1. **Sub-Stepping Updates:** The 60 Hz timestep ![][image83] is split into ![][image84] sub-steps (![][image85]), raising the effective collision evaluation frequency to ![][image86]18.  
> 2. **Swept-AABB Raycast Projections:** Prior to integrating positions, the engine casts a ray along the projectile's projected velocity vector ![][image87]. If an intersection with a static collider occurs, the engine clamps the projectile position to the contact point and triggers the collision resolution pipeline1.

### **6.3 Collision Resolution Pipeline and Code Implementation**

The physics loop listens to Matter.js collisionStart events to calculate impact energy, trigger fragment spawning, adjust score multipliers, add screen trauma, and send asynchronous AI events3.

JavaScript  
// Dynamic Physics Collision Event Pipeline  
Matter.Events.on(engine, 'collisionStart', (event) \=\> {  
    const pairs \= event.pairs; // Iterate through collision pairs \[cite: 19\]  
      
    for (let i \= 0; i \< pairs.length; i++) {  
        const { bodyA, bodyB } \= pairs\[i\];  
          
        // Isolate projectile and target references  
        const ball \= bodyA.label \=== 'projectile' ? bodyA : (bodyB.label \=== 'projectile' ? bodyB : null);  
        const target \= ball \=== bodyA ? bodyB : bodyA;  
          
        if (ball && target) {  
            // Compute relative impact velocity vector  
            const relVelX \= ball.velocity.x \- target.velocity.x;  
            const relVelY \= ball.velocity.y \- target.velocity.y;  
            const relSpeedSq \= relVelX \* relVelX \+ relVelY \* relVelY;  
              
            // Calculate transferred kinetic energy  
            const impactEnergy \= 0.5 \* ball.mass \* relSpeedSq;  
              
            // Evaluate destruction state trigger  
            if (target.isDestructible && impactEnergy \> target.breakThreshold) {  
                // Instanciate broken fragment meshes  
                breakObjectIntoFragments(world, target);  
                  
                // Increment render camera trauma  
                addScreenTrauma(target.traumaContribution);  
                  
                // Calculate and apply score with active multiplier  
                scoreEngine.addPoints(target.pointValue \* comboSystem.currentMultiplier);  
                  
                // Stream event telemetry payload to Edge LLM worker  
                dispatchEdgeAIEventPayload({  
                    npc\_id: target.associatedNpcId,  
                    impact\_object: target.objectName,  
                    combo\_multiplier: comboSystem.currentMultiplier,  
                    ball\_type: ball.ballType,  
                    ball\_velocity: Math.sqrt(relSpeedSq)  
                });  
            }  
        }  
    }  
});

The rendering loop extracts physics transforms, applies camera offsets, and draws bodies to the HTML5 canvas context each frame2:

JavaScript  
// Main Render Synchronization Loop  
function renderLoop(currentTime) {  
    const deltaTime \= (currentTime \- lastTime) / 1000;  
    lastTime \= currentTime;  
      
    // Clear canvas viewport  
    ctx.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);  
      
    // Compute current camera offset from trauma  
    const cameraOffset \= updateCameraShake(deltaTime);  
      
    ctx.save();  
    // Apply translational and rotational shake transforms  
    ctx.translate(cameraOffset.x, cameraOffset.y);  
    ctx.rotate(cameraOffset.angle);  
      
    // Draw active bodies in the physics world  
    const bodies \= Matter.Composite.allBodies(world);  
    for (let i \= 0; i \< bodies.length; i++) {  
        const body \= bodies\[i\];  
        drawBody(ctx, body);  
    }  
      
    ctx.restore();  
      
    // Request next animation frame  
    requestAnimationFrame(renderLoop);  
}

## **7\. Strategic Conclusions and System Specifications**

The architecture of *Backyard Havoc* shows how accessible arcade timing mechanics can be expanded through physical destruction systems and dynamic edge AI dialogue5. Sub-stepped physics integration keeps high-velocity juggling inputs stable3, while trauma-based camera shake adds strong visual feedback without throwing off tap precision9. Sub-200ms edge LLM pipelines turn static environments into reactive cartoon scenes7, delivering a scalable foundation for ongoing monetization and high player retention11.
